provisions.title: Indiana Consumer Data Protection Act: controller duties, processing of sensitive data
provisions.quote: A controller shall not process sensitive data concerning a consumer without obtaining the consumer's consent
provisions.appliesTo: Persons that "controls or processes personal data of at least one hundred thousand (100,000) consumers who are Indiana residents", or 25,000 with over 50% of revenue from sale (IC 24-15-1-1). HIPAA covered entities and business associates are exempt.

provisions.title: Indiana Consumer Data Protection Act: definition of sensitive data
provisions.quote: a mental or physical health diagnosis made by a health care provider
provisions.appliesTo: Same thresholds as IC 24-15-1-1.

provisions.title: Consumer genetic testing providers: acts requiring consent
provisions.quote: may not take any of the following actions unless the provider has solicited and received the individual's freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous consent to the action:
provisions.appliesTo: Consumer genetic testing providers (IC 24-4-24-2). Excludes testing ordered by a health care provider and subject to HIPAA (IC 24-4-24-1(b)).

consumer_health_data.note: IC 24-15, effective 1 January 2026, requires consent to process sensitive data, which includes a health diagnosis by a provider. HIPAA entities are exempt. No dedicated consumer health data law found. Act effective date read from SEA 5 enrolled text.

resolution.by: editor rulings drafted by an agent against primary sources, approved by J. A. Snyder under delegation

freeCopyCases: Copy of or access to the patient's x-ray image, at no cost, for the patient or designee (IC 16-39-1-2)
Digital copy or digital access through an interoperability platform of an electronic health record (IC 16-39-9-2(1))
feeRules: IC 16-39-9-2: "A provider may not charge a person for: (1) providing a digital copy or digital access through an interoperability platform of an individual's electronic health record; or (2) making and providing paper copies of medical records at an amount greater than the amount set in rules"
Paper copy amounts are set by Department of Insurance rule under IC 16-39-9-4. Rule text not read in this session.

provisions.title: X-rays: copy or access at no cost
provisions.quote: a provider shall, at no cost, provide to the patient or the patient's designee: (1) access to; or (2) a copy of; the patient's x-ray image possessed by the provider.
provisions.appliesTo: Any provider holding the patient's x-ray image.

provisions.title: Right of access; deadline for written requests
provisions.quote: a provider shall provide the health records requested under this section within thirty (30) days after the date the written request is made
provisions.appliesTo: Providers, for all health records except mental health records, communicable disease records and 42 CFR Part 2 records. One 30-day extension is allowed.

provisions.title: Fees for records
provisions.quote: A provider may not charge a person for: (1) providing a digital copy or digital access through an interoperability platform of an individual's electronic health record; or (2) making and providing paper copies of medical records at an amount greater than the amount set in rules
provisions.appliesTo: Providers.

leads.usedFor: Located the Department of Insurance copy fee rule, 760 IAC 1-71 (not used as evidence)

copy_rights.note: Free x-ray image copy for the patient or designee goes beyond the HIPAA cost-based fee. The deadline is 30 days plus one 30-day extension, equal to HIPAA. Free digital copy alone would not count under Ruling D-1.

crossCheck.note: beyondFederalFloor yes: free x-ray copy goes beyond HIPAA fees. Deadline is 30 days, not shorter. P.L.215-2025 effective July 1, 2025 and P.L.196-2021 effective July 1, 2021, per Acts. Fee amounts in 760 IAC 1-71 not recorded.

hie_consent.designatedHie: Indiana Health Information Exchange (IHIE), named by the state as its primary HIE

leads.usedFor: Reported that IHIE participants follow an opt-out policy; not confirmed on a primary page

hie_consent.note: Searched Titles 4, 12, 16, 24 and 27 indexes. No HIE consent statute found. A state page calls IHIE the state's primary HIE, not designated. No published IHIE patient opt-out policy found. IC 16-39-5-1 allows provider record requests without consent.

crossCheck.note: My search of Title 16 and Title 12 PDFs for health information exchange found no consent rule. The state page calls IHIE primary, not designated. IHIE pages I opened show no opt-out policy.

designatedHieSources.title: Grow Rural Health, Initiative 3 FAQ (Indiana)
designatedHieSources.citation: in.gov Grow Rural Health Initiative 3 page, FAQ "What is an HIE?"
designatedHieSources.quote: The Indiana Health Information Exchange (IHIE), founded in 2004, is the state's primary HIE.

designatedHieSources.title: IHIE home page
designatedHieSources.citation: Indiana Health Information Exchange home page
designatedHieSources.quote: IHIE combines, enhances, and exchanges health data across all care settings to support treatment, care coordination, quality improvement, and public and population health.

provisions.title: Abortion reports: quarterly public report, no identifying information
provisions.quote: The state department shall ensure that no identifying information of a pregnant woman is contained in the report.
provisions.appliesTo: Department of Health reports compiled from abortion reports filed by health care providers.

reproductive.note: IC 16-34-2-5 bars identifying information of the pregnant woman in the public report built from abortion reports. IC 16-34-2-4(i) makes court records of minor consent waiver proceedings confidential.

crossCheck.note: Quote is in IC 16-34-2-5(e). Last amendment P.L.56-2023, listed as effective 7/1/2023 in the 2023 Enrolled Act Summary. IC 16-34-2-4(i) also makes waiver proceeding court records confidential.

provisions.title: Mental health records: confidentiality
provisions.quote: A patient's mental health record is confidential and shall be disclosed only with the consent of the patient unless otherwise provided in the following:
provisions.appliesTo: Mental health records held by providers (IC 16-39-2-1).

mental_health.note: Text unchanged since P.L.2-1993, approved 30 April 1993 with no section date, so July 1, 1993 under IC 1-1-3-3. Exceptions are listed in IC 16-39-2, 16-39-3, 16-39-4 and 16-39-5-3.

crossCheck.note: IC 16-39-2-3 history shows only P.L.2-1993. IC 16-18-3-4 states SEA 24 of 1993 took effect July 1, 1993, matching the researcher's date.

provisions.title: Prenatal HIV tests: results confidential
provisions.quote: (g) The results of a test performed under section 5 or 6 of this chapter are confidential.
provisions.appliesTo: A physician or advanced practice registered nurse who orders an HIV test for a pregnant woman under IC 16-41-6-5 or 16-41-6-6.

provisions.title: Communicable disease information: confidentiality
provisions.quote: a person may not disclose or be compelled to disclose medical or epidemiological information involving a communicable disease or other serious disease
provisions.appliesTo: Diseases on the list published under IC 16-41-2-1. Release allowed with written consent of each person identified, among other listed cases.

hiv.note: IC 16-41-6-8 names HIV tests. IC 16-41-8-1 covers listed communicable diseases. IC 16-39-1-1(b) routes communicable disease records to IC 16-41-8-1.

crossCheck.note: 2018 Acts show P.L.129-2018 amending IC 16-41-6-8 effective July 1, 2018. 2025 Acts show P.L.143-2025 amending IC 16-41-8-1 effective July 1, 2025.

provisions.title: Consumer genetic testing providers: third party access requires consent
provisions.quote: (3) Subject to section 10(b) of this chapter, provide access by a third party to: (A) the individual's biological material; or (B) data, other than deidentified data, resulting from genetic testing performed on the individual's biological material.
provisions.appliesTo: Consumer genetic testing providers. Excludes testing ordered by a health care provider and subject to HIPAA.

genetic.note: IC 24-4-24-9 requires separate consent for third party access. IC 24-4-24-10(b) bars giving data to insurers or employers even with consent. P.L.233-2025 took effect on passage, approved 6 May 2025.

crossCheck.note: 2025 Acts show P.L.233-2025 (HEA 1521) approved May 6, 2025, with IC 24-4-24 effective upon passage and an emergency declared. IC 16-39-5-2(d) also requires separate written consent for insurers to obtain genetic test results.

facts.statutoryDamages: None for individuals. Attorney general civil penalty up to $7,500 per violation under IC 24-15-10-2 and IC 24-4-24-11.

provisions.title: Indiana Consumer Data Protection Act: no private right of action
provisions.quote: Nothing in this article shall be construed as providing the basis for a private right of action for violations of this article or any other law.
provisions.appliesTo: Controllers and processors under IC 24-15.

provisions.title: Consumer genetic testing providers: enforcement
provisions.quote: Nothing in this section may be construed as providing the basis for a private right of action for violations of this chapter or any other law.
provisions.appliesTo: Consumer genetic testing providers.

provisions.title: Security breach disclosure: enforcement
provisions.quote: commits a deceptive act that is actionable only by the attorney general under this chapter.
provisions.appliesTo: Persons required to disclose a breach under IC 24-4.9-3.

private_right.note: Indiana's privacy, genetic testing and breach laws give enforcement to the attorney general only. No civil action found in IC 16-39 or IC 16-41-8, which use fines, discipline and misdemeanors.

crossCheck.note: IC 24-4-24-11 and IC 27-8-26-10 also give enforcement to the attorney general or the commissioner. I found no civil action in IC 16-39 or IC 16-41-8. The 2009 enrolled HEA 1121 shows IC 24-4.9-4-1 effective July 1, 2009.

facts.noticeDeadline: Without unreasonable delay, not more than 45 days after discovery (IC 24-4.9-3-3)

provisions.title: Definition of personal information
provisions.quote: one (1) or more of the following data elements that are not encrypted or redacted: (A) A driver's license number. (B) A state identification card number. (C) A credit card number.
provisions.appliesTo: Data base owners doing business in Indiana.

provisions.title: Timing of disclosure
provisions.quote: shall make the disclosure or notification without unreasonable delay, but not more than forty-five (45) days after the discovery of the breach.
provisions.appliesTo: Persons required to disclose under IC 24-4.9-3.

provisions.title: Disclosure of breach to the attorney general
provisions.quote: If a data base owner makes a disclosure described in subsection (a), the data base owner shall also disclose the breach to the attorney general.
provisions.appliesTo: Data base owners.

provisions.title: Own disclosure procedures under federal law, including HIPAA
provisions.quote: (6) the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) (P.L. 104-191); is not required to make a disclosure under this chapter
provisions.appliesTo: Data base owners whose HIPAA compliance plan requires notice without unreasonable delay and who follow it.

breach_health.note: Personal information covers Social Security, driver's license, state ID, card and account numbers, and adult website data. Medical and health insurance information are not listed.

crossCheck.note: The IC 24-4.9-2-10 definition omits medical and health insurance information. Acts confirm these effective dates: July 1, 2024 (P.L.98-2024), July 1, 2022 (P.L.171-2022), July 1, 2026 (P.L.23-2026 SEC.247) and July 1, 2009.

prohibitions: IC 27-1-52-9(b): "A provider may not use an automated: (1) process; (2) system; or (3) tool, including artificial intelligence; to submit a health benefits claim without the review of a provider or other person involved in the development of the claim for submission."

provisions.title: Downcoding: limit on automated process, system or tool
provisions.quote: as the sole basis to downcode a claim based on medical necessity without the review of the covered individual's medical record by an employee or contractor of the insurer.
provisions.appliesTo: Insurers issuing accident and sickness policies, HMOs, dental PPO insurers and their contractors. Not Medicaid or Medicaid managed care (IC 27-1-52-0.3).

provisions.title: Disclosure of AI use in prior authorization denials and downcoding
provisions.quote: An insurer must disclose in an easily accessible and readable manner when artificial intelligence is used to: (1) make an adverse determination on a prior authorization request; or (2) downcode a claim.
provisions.appliesTo: Same insurers as IC 27-1-52-9(a).

ai_care.note: Counted: AI may not be the sole basis to downcode a claim. Not counted: 9(c) covers coverage decisions, not care communication or diagnosis, and names no recipient. Provider appeals in 27-1-52-12 are not patient recourse.

crossCheck.note: 2026 Acts show P.L.88-2026 (HEA 1271) adding IC 27-1-52 effective July 1, 2026. The 9(c) disclosure covers coverage decisions only. Appeals in section 12 are for providers. HB 1620 (2025) does not appear in the 2025 Acts.
